Furthermore, practitioners could leverage the model to aid strategic interventions for business and policy outcomes.

articleTitle: A Sustainable Approach for Multiple Dwellings Development Through Joint Procurement
abstract: Infrastructure and construction projects majorly contribute to the national economy of developing nations. Development strategies in such upbound moves in the construction industry need to align with the housing system improvement models. Joint procurement (JP) of resources and services results in sharing of resources, costs, and energy requirements. This perspective article aims to figure out critical parameters of JP for the medium level construction businesses in India and reveals that such an approach would seriously consider economic growth, sustainable quality life, and increasing per capita income. Bridging the knowledge gap between disperse stakeholders through JP methods would give rise to a new construction approach when support and cooperation between all the stakeholders exist. The JP model's adoption gives further initiatives to minimize the detrimental impacts of construction on the environment and society, besides developing a sustainability outlook and performance within the community.

articleTitle: Worldwide Pandemic Impacts: A Malaysian Case Study
abstract: This widespread pandemic has wreaked on the shipping and maritime industries not only in China, but also in ports around the world. Maritime is not resistant to pandemics, and it is much more difficult to manage due to the dynamic surface. That is why Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) was developed to more efficiently administer, assess, and monitor all marine activities. The aim of this the study is to analyze the pandemic from the standpoint of the pros and cons to the Malaysia as maritime country. This study used a variety of sample papers as references to reveal information from an engineering database. It is then divided into four segment: port management, transportation, marine life, and supply chain. Each segment will be examined in greater depth using qualitative analysis. The findings highlight the significance of incorporating MSP into trade strategies for sustainable and efficient marine resource management, fostering economic growth, and promoting environmental sustainability. Additionally, it suggests potential quantitative projections for future researchers, including trade volume growth, economic and environmental impacts, infrastructure investments, and risk assessments. In conclusion, this research emphasizes the importance of incorporating MSP into trade planning strategies to ensure sustainable and efficient utilization of marine resources.

articleTitle: Visualizing Portfolios: Prompt Discussions and Provoke Debates in Management Meetings
abstract: Portfolio perspectives are fundamental for executives, and visual approaches provide an accessible means of conveying summary overviews and in-depth depictions of projects, programs, and platforms. However, within organizations, the design of such charts, diagrams, and graphs is relatively poor. Given the importance of portfolios, visualizations should be more thoughtfully designed to better present information in expressive ways while ensuring an appropriate balance of data provision aligned with the needs of the audience/viewers. Visuals are not merely a method of reporting, they can also be strategically deployed to support decision-making. Visualizations can be used to trigger and structure the necessary conversations between managers and executives, enabling much-needed discussions and even healthy debates. This article presents a selection of visuals that were developed to depict different types and aspects of portfolios as a means to prompt meaningful and constructive dialog among key stakeholders—especially in management meetings (either online or in-person). These visualizations act as exemplars of new and novel practices in leading organizations and provide both useful representations and inspiration for other companies.

articleTitle: Defining Indicators for Performance Evaluation in Science and Technology Parks
abstract: Performance evaluation is highly relevant, given the importance of science and technology parks for developing and disseminating knowledge and innovation. In this sense, this article sought to validate indicators for evaluating the performance of science and technology parks in the Brazilian context. To achieve the proposed objective, 213 indicators were selected, divided into ten assessment areas, and validated by 15 experts in the field. Our findings revealed that, from the total number of indicators selected, 136 were validated, drawing attention to the parks’ relational area, which had the most indicators, both in the literature analyzed and in the validation process. Hence, this article provides theoretical and practical contributions that, through empirical data, can help evaluate performance and develop the management of science and technology parks since applying validated indicators can generate pertinent information, help articulate strategies, and promote innovation and entrepreneurship.

articleTitle: Challenges of value co-creation in the digital era: a study of supply chain partners
abstract: Because of rapid advances in information technology, firms are facing challenges in providing value to their customers and are struggling to co-create value in their supply chains. The purpose of this study, which was theoretically based on value co-creation, was to investigate the key explicit and implicit drivers of value co-creation by supply chain partners. Semistructured interviews and a case study of a supply chain comprising five companies were used to gather the primary data. This study discovered strategies that can help firms cultivate internal and external linkages, particularly as they relate to information sharing. This study contributes to value co-creation theory in digital transformation in the context of linkages among supply chain partners. This study highlights the role and importance of customer and supplier engagement in value co-creation. The findings reveal the operational strategy, functional resources, and digital transformation that give rise to value co-creation between supply chain partners. This study contributes to value co-creation theory regarding digital transformation in the context of linkages between supply chain partners

articleTitle: Automatic Learning for Commercial Registration Renewal—The Case of Camara de Comercio of Barranquilla-Colombia
abstract: This article shows the implementation of a prediction model of the payment behavior of the renewal concept of companies registered in the commercial registry of the Barranquilla Chamber of Commerce using machine learning techniques in a multilevel classification scenario, where it will offer the organization a tool that allows it to know in advance the behavior of the payment of the renewal of a company in such a way that it is able to design strategies to increase the success indicators in terms of the number of registration renewals, mercantile, and of the income collected for this concept.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Engineering Management—An Editor's Perspective (2023)
abstract: Today, we live in a world determined by multiple crises creating less certainty about the future and its prediction. At the same time, new Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies are developed at high pace that may lead to a new revolution in how we do business and manage companies. Generative AI tools offer exciting opportunities while at the same time putting to question some well-established solutions. This calls for more and extensive insights in research and practice to tackle the question how these technologies can be used for engineering management.

articleTitle: Transitions – IEEE Engineering Management Review in 2023
Guest Editorial AI-Driven Decision-Making: Managerial and Organizational Promise and Potential
abstract: TO remain competitive, every business requires useful information and knowledge. Identifying the target audience, understanding what consumers want, and anticipating their requirements are critical components of organizational management, decision-making, and planning processes. Appropriate data processing and analysis help firms attain these objectives while thriving in an uncertain and dynamic environment.

articleTitle: Editorial Transformative Learning as a Catalyst for Innovation in Times of Uncertainty
abstract: The significance of innovations, in uncertain times we live in, continues to grow. Innovations are needed not only to address diverse challenges but also for the development of new sustainable outcomes. Technological advancements, including artificial intelligence, societal challenges, and crises, pose multifaceted issues in the workplace, demanding a diverse expertise for resolution. Therefore, the competence, knowledge, and ability to learn adaptively and transformatively by professionals play a central role in innovation. In this issue of IEEE Engineering Management Review (EMR), we explore various aspects of innovations, transformation, and learning. It is crucial to encompass such a wide array of topics to reflect on these issues and provide guidance on tackling them. The message conveyed is clear: never cease to learn and refine your approach to managing, developing, and facing challenges.

articleTitle: “Crazy Days”: Engineering Management in Times of Crisis Innovation
The Benefits of a Good Company Tour: Insights From Walking Around
abstract: Touring corporate facilities can provide insights to many issues and practices. In this article we provide some general insights into information that can be gleaned from plant tours by various stakeholders. Whether it is internal employees, external actors such as suppliers and customers, or even educational tours, various learning can occur. We provide some examples of insights gained from some company tours and how it can be useful to managers and educators or scholars.

articleTitle: IEEE Engineering Management Review—Call for Technology Manager's Notebook Articles (2023)
abstract: Interested in publishing in an IEEE journal, but do not have the time to write a long and in-depth manuscript? <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">IEEE Engineering Management Review</small> (EMR) offers authors the opportunity to submit Technology Manager's Notebook (TMN) articles to share their insights in management of engineering and technology. This is not only particularly designed for industry practitioners but also for researchers who are experts in a field who want to summarize their key insights. We call these evidence-based articles where authors reflect upon their personal experiences on a certain topic. Experience is not necessarily a matter of age but of interesting and useful insights.
